I think a mod is a ministry of defence, according to altavista.

A mod is like a debate leader for the subvoat. He makes sure everybody gets a say in an orderly fashion and in order of severity either warns users, removes offensive posts or bans users from participating if they break the pre-agreed rules. In some situations the mod do a case by case evaluation in his rulings, but mostly it's just enforcing the rules making a mod more like a janitor than a judge and jury.

Beyond having a hand and say in how the subvoat is run, the mod check post submissions and comments for unwanted content - normally such things as profanity, personal attacks and illegal stuff.

The power of the mods, beyond the obvious removal of posts or comments lies in controling the dialogue. Effectively being able to remove any discussion about mods removing discussions poses a transparacy problem and abuse of the mod position and networking between the mods have led to several episodes of mass migration from reddit to voat.
